newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China province urges drug peddlars to surrender.
newsitem.headline: China province urges drug peddlars to surrender.

text.p: China's Guangdong province has called on drug traffickers to turn themselves in or risk becoming the target of a government crackdown, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily said on Monday.

Officials in the southern province have announced a deadline of June 26 for dealers to surrender to the government as part of an anti-drug campaign carried out nationwide to help maintain social stability, the newspaper said.
Anyone who trafficks, transports, sells, makes or illegally holds drugs must turn themselves in by the deadline, it said, quoting a provincial government directive issued on Sunday.
Those who cause people to take drugs or who protect drug criminals must also surrender by June 26, the directive said.
It did not say whether people who voluntarily surrender will face less severe penalties.
A police source in southern China said drug-related crimes were punished severely, with penalties ranging up to death.
Drug addicts must register with the police by June 10 for detoxification treatment, the directive said, adding those who resumed use after treatment would be sentenced to education through labour.
The People's Daily, mouthpiece of China's ruling Communist Party, in March quoted the country's top police official, Tao Siju, as calling for tougher efforts to combat drugs.
Tao, Minister of Public Security, warned that dealers were increasingly dangerous and the problem was spinning out of control.
Drug abuse, virtually eradicated after the Communists came to power in 1949, has staged a comeback as market-oriented reforms have loosened Beijing's control over people's lives.
